stories.title: GlobalFoundries becomes the first non-automotive customer to test Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid
paragraphs: Boston Dynamics announced on Nov. 17, 2026, that semiconductor maker GlobalFoundries will be the first semiconductor manufacturer to test humanoid robots through the Atlas early adopter program, while also deploying more Spot robots across its global manufacturing network. The Robot Report reports that GlobalFoundries is the first customer outside the automotive industry to test Atlas, with testing set to begin in early 2027.

According to the companies, two Spot robots at GlobalFoundries' Singapore facility have traveled nearly 900 kilometers and completed more than 90,000 inspections in sub-fab areas since April, with a 99% mission success rate. The Robot Report says the companies will identify humanoid applications in chip manufacturing and begin training Atlas on specific tasks, but did not disclose how many robots, which facilities or which first tasks are involved.

The Robot Report notes that Boston Dynamics' initial Atlas production for 2026 was committed to its parent company Hyundai and to Google DeepMind, and that Hyundai has outlined plans to deploy 25,000 Atlas humanoids across Hyundai Motor and Kia plants over the next several years.

image.credit: Boston Dynamics, via The Robot Report

stories.title: Agility Robotics names a new president and product chief after its Nasdaq listing
paragraphs: Agility Robotics, maker of the Digit humanoid, announced three executive appointments on Nov. 18, 2026. Daniel Diez, previously Chief Business Officer, was promoted to President; Christopher "Sully" Sullivan, who joined in May as Vice President of Customer Success, became Chief Product Officer; and Ana Lang, previously Chief Legal & People Officer, was named Chief Administrative Officer.

The company says the appointments follow its Nov. 4 completion of a business combination with Churchill Capital Corp XI and its listing on Nasdaq under the symbol AGLT. Agility also points to the unveiling of Digit 5 in September, an expanded deployment agreement with GXO, a planned pilot with AGCO, and paid evaluation programs with three more manufacturing customers announced in October.

According to the release, Diez secured more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5, which the company describes as potential multi-year value subject to contractual milestones and product specifications. As Chief Product Officer, Sullivan will oversee Digit, Agility Arc and future products while continuing to lead customer success.

stories.title: Humyn Labs raises $47 million to collect real-world training data for robots
paragraphs: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs announced a $47 million Series A on Nov. 18, 2026, made up of $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton, The Robot Report and TechCrunch report. The company collects data on how people perform tasks to help AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers train robots for the real world.

TechCrunch reports that Humyn Labs uses its own two-camera hardware to record people doing everyday tasks, then processes and labels the footage, collecting data in more than 20 countries in Latin America and Asia, with Brazil, India and South Korea as main hubs. Co-founder Ishank Gupta told The Robot Report the company gathers data across vision, sound, touch and motion and works across robot types, from arms to mobile robots.

The Robot Report says the company reported more than $50 million in annualized revenue within six months of operations. TechCrunch reports co-founder Manish Agarwal said it generated $10 million in revenue between April and October with another $20 million in signed contracts, and that it has 12 paying customers, with about 90% of revenue from the U.S. TechCrunch also notes that recording people inside their homes has raised privacy and consent questions across this kind of data collection.

image.credit: Humyn Labs, via The Robot Report
